question: Does the observed FV-over-FIII source-classified initiation-rate ordering remain even if every short-follow-up noninitiator with inadequate receiver evidence were an unseen initiator? How many additional longer-observed negative labels would have to be wrong to erase the pooled ordering?

admissible_scenarios.A: All 422 source initiation positives remain positive. Only the existing 100 short-followup source negatives are allowed to be hypothesized as unobserved initiators, independently by project and stage. The 53 day-90-supported negatives are retained as negative. This gives sharp algebraic bounds, not statistical confidence intervals or biological estimates.
admissible_scenarios.B: Starting from the worst-case Scenario A for FIII and the original FV observed initiation count, reassign the minimum number of FIII day-90-supported source negative labels to initiation needed for the pooled FIII rate to match or exceed the original FV rate. No re-training or extrapolation.
admissible_scenarios.C: Compute project-specific FIII/FV bounds on the same restrictions and count each strict robust positive, strict robust negative, and ambiguous/equality project; do not aggregate signs as if independent replication.

required_checks: Exactly 422 original source-classified initiators; exactly 100 short-followup negatives plus 53 day90-supported negatives.
For every stage and project, ambiguous short-followup counts never exceed original source negatives; project counts reconcile stage totals.
FV minus FIII pooled lower bound computed with all FIII short-followup negatives flipped and no FV negatives flipped; upper with inverse assignment.
Strict bound >0 permits ordering ONLY conditional on Scenario A, not true observed physiological initiation.
Compute minimum extra flips in longer-observed FIII negatives by exact rational/integer arithmetic; this is a vulnerability threshold, NOT their empirical misclassification count.
Project aggregation may exhibit Simpson-like composition; report project-specific upper/lower and opposing strata.
unsupported_claims: Observed telemetry noninitiation is not verified biological inactivity.
90-day receiver observation is not proof of continuous detection opportunity.
Condition effects are not established by silvering-stage marginal bounds.
Pooled stage ranking does not establish a causal stage effect or universal cross-waterway ordering.
Sharp bounds conditional on limited label ambiguity are not sampling confidence intervals.
